title: Great Question's 2025 Year-in-Review
summary: A year of releases (AI moderation, card sorting, tree testing), 14,166 studies and 51,802 interviews booked, customer stories, and 120% headcount growth. Great Question's 2025 in review.
body_markdown:
2025 has been a pivotal year at Great Question for both the product and the people who shape it.


Yes, we released a ton of new features, from[card sorting](https://www.greatquestion.com/features/card-sorting) and[tree testing](https://www.greatquestion.com/features/tree-testing) to[AI-moderated interviews](https://www.greatquestion.com/features/ai-moderated-interviews) and our[User Interviews integration](https://www.greatquestion.com/features/user-interviews-integration) , all to advance our mission of helping teams democratize research at scale.


But along the way, we also grew headcount 120% with 30 great hires across every department (and seven countries), while our incredible customers collectively booked over 50,000 user interviews in Great Question.


To cap it all off, we recently announced our[$13M Series A fundraising round](https://www.greatquestion.com/blog/series-a) led by Inovia Capital, with participation from Character Capital, January Capital, and Y Combinator.


With 2026 just around the corner, let's recap the year that was at Great Question.


## 🚀 Product releases & user activity


In 2025, our customers published a total of **14,166 research studies** in Great Question, a 73% increase from 2024. That's not just researchers: that's designers, product managers, marketers, and other teams running their own research. Across these studies, you booked a total of **51,802 customer interviews** , a 50% increase from 2024. You're talking to customers more than ever, and our scheduling and calendar tools are making it easier.


To thank their research participants for their time and feedback, **87,263 research incentives were sent** , a 111% increase from 2024. More participants, more studies, more insight. And here's the one that really matters: **514,258 artifacts viewed by your teams** , up 60% from last year. That means insights aren't sitting in a repository gathering dust. They're being found, shared, and used to make decisions.


Meanwhile, our team shipped some huge product updates, like:


### AI moderated interviews


Our biggest release of 2025,[AI moderation](https://www.greatquestion.com/features/ai-moderated-interviews) combines the best of both worlds: the scale of a survey with the depth of an interview. Define your research objectives and topics, and our AI moderator can interview hundreds of participants in parallel across time zones and without scheduling overhead or bandwidth bottlenecks. This isn't just another chatbot, it's research-grade AI that adapts in real time, probing for detail and capturing nuance to deliver the depth you'd normally only get from live moderation. Every transcript, highlight reel, and insight is automatically stored in your[repository](https://www.greatquestion.com/features/research-repository) .


Learn more


[Book an AI moderation demo](https://www.greatquestion.com/demo-request?utm_source=2025-review-ai-moderation)


[Watch a quick overview](https://www.loom.com/share/8bdbb8a17654410c834275bd92d3c8ae)


[Read our AI moderation guide](https://www.greatquestion.com/ux-research/ai-moderation)


### Card sorting


This year, we strengthened our suite of mixed method tools with the addition of[card sorting](https://www.greatquestion.com/features/card-sorting) . Now you can run open, closed, or hybrid card sorts to better understand how users naturally categorize information, spot hidden patterns and misalignments in user mental models, and analyze results with agreement matrices. Card sorting complements the moderated and unmoderated methods you already use in Great Question, and brings us one step closer to solving the deeper workflow challenge we're obsessed with: removing the need for tool switching by keeping every step of the research process connected in one place.


Learn more


[Book a card sorting demo](https://www.greatquestion.com/demo-request?utm_source=2025-review-card-sorting)


[Watch a founder demo](https://www.tella.tv/video/cmabkidpo000b0bk026gm5znm/view)


[Read our launch announcement](https://www.greatquestion.com/blog/introducing-card-sorting-in-great-question)


[Read our card sorting guide](https://www.greatquestion.com/ux-research/card-sorting)


### Tree testing


Whereas card sorting helps you understand how users naturally group and label content,[tree testing](https://www.greatquestion.com/features/tree-testing) validates whether users can find what they're looking for within your structure. They go hand in hand when designing and evaluating an information architecture, which is why we brought them together under one roof. Assign tasks to see how users navigate your structure, surface what works and where users get lost, and validate before launch with clear task results and success data.


Learn more


[Book a tree testing demo](https://www.greatquestion.com/demo-request?utm_source=2025-review-tree-testing)


[Watch a founder demo](https://www.tella.tv/video/structuring-your-navigation-gnov)


[Read our launch announcement](https://www.greatquestion.com/ux-research/tree-testing-guide)


### User Interviews integration


Great Question already has everything you need for research with your own users. So, it's about time we teamed up with the best external panel provider in the biz, now you can access 6M+ verified participants from[User Interviews](https://www.greatquestion.com/features/user-interviews-integration) , right in Great Question. This partnership doubles the external panel size of our previous provider, with a one-hour first match guarantee, 400M+ data points for targeting niche audiences, and rigorous fraud detection (<0.6% fraud rate). The result is better quality, greater reach, and more predictable pricing for everyone.


Learn more


[Book a User Interviews integration demo](https://www.greatquestion.com/demo-request?utm_source=2025-review-ui-integration)


[Read our launch announcement](https://www.greatquestion.com/blog/user-interviews-x-great-question-a-partnership-for-higher-quality-research)


### Smarter screeners


While new methods and integrations grab the headlines, our smarter screeners might be the unsung hero of Great Question's 2025 lineup. Finding the right participants is now easier than ever: set qualification rules upfront, then let automation handle the sorting. Tag answers as qualifying or disqualifying, and route participants with branching logic. Automatically approve qualified participants while others can be automatically screened out to a customizable disqualification page. Review your screener logic in one panel and see qualification status when crafting invites.


Learn more


[Watch a quick overview](https://youtu.be/dF2EMjZlAuQ)


[Sign up to try it for yourself](https://greatquestion.co/users/sign_up?utm_source=2025-review-screeners&source=www_greatquestion_com)


### Democratized pricing


Our customers are proving that research democratization isn't just our vision anymore.[Asana](https://asana.com/) went from a handful of researchers to company-wide participation.[Brex](https://www.brex.com/) put customer conversations in the hands of PMs, designers, and engineers.[ServiceNow](https://www.servicenow.com/) runs 300+ studies a year, connecting with over 10,000 end users across research, design, and product teams. This is what happens when research evolves from something handled by a few to something embedded across the company, with the right guardrails in place. Our new democratized pricing supports that: helping your team scale research responsibly, without trading rigor for access.[Book a meeting to explore democratizing pricing for your team.](https://www.greatquestion.com/demo-request)


### Smaller, impactful features


-


**Ask AI for Unmoderated Studies.** Chat with any response, or the entire study. Ask follow-up questions, dig into specific patterns, or generate summaries instantly.


-


**Matrix questions for surveys.** Rate feature satisfaction, likelihood to recommend services, or agreement with statements in one clean format participants recognize.


-


**Role-based permissions.** Control who can add or export candidates, create studies, enable livestreams, recruit participants, and more. Perfect for enterprise compliance.


-


**Feature access control.** Toggle features on or off across your workspace and ensure your governance policies are fully enforced while democratizing research.


-


**SSO authentication.** Set up SAML-only workspaces so your team never sees a password field again. Great for security teams who need thorough documentation.


-


**PDF repository support.** Upload reports and docs directly to your repository. View, download, tag, and search PDFs like any other artifact, keeping all your research context in one place.


-


**Frictionless unmoderated testing.** We redesigned the participant experience with a collapsible top bar for instructions, giving your prototypes center stage and eliminating distractions.


-


**Images settings for unmoderated studies.** Choose how uploaded images display in unmoderated studies with fit-to-width, actual size, or other sizing options.


-


**See "now" in any timezone view.** See exactly where "now" sits in your calendar with a live time indicator. Perfect for global distributed teams.


-


**Enhanced tables.** Updates to the Candidates, Studies, and Participants tables make for a faster, smoother experience when loading, filtering, and searching.


-


**Databricks integration.** Connect and import candidates from Databricks to simplify participant management and accelerate your research process.


-


**Preview your test from your currently selected task.** View your entire unmoderated test or just the current block you're working on.


-


**Ensure participants record the right screen.** Our screen-sharing dialog ensures participants always record the right content for high-quality responses every time.


-


**Improved study alerts.** Catch events that could prevent candidates from participating in your studies, like past calendar dates, disconnected integrations, and candidate eligibility.


-


**More unmoderated testing improvements.** Give every participant a great experience with features like microphone detection, end task confirmation, and prototype view settings.


For quality-of-life improvements and regular product release updates,[check out our changelog](https://greatquestion.co/support/releases-updates/changelog) .


## 🍺 Customer froth: case studies & testimonials


We believe every team should be able to talk to customers, test ideas, and make decisions grounded in customer truth. That's why we're building a world where research isn't a department, it's a habit. And some of the world's most innovative companies are joining us. From global enterprises to scale-ups, hundreds of teams use Great Question to integrate research into their everyday workflow. They're proving what happens when research becomes part of company culture: faster learning, smarter decisions, and products that reflect what customers actually need.


### Asana


At Asana, Great Question enables one ResearchOps pro to serve 45 teams: removing the bottlenecks that slow research down, enabling product managers and designers to run their own studies with confidence, and maintaining enterprise compliance every step of the way.


> “Great Question has been instrumental in democratizing our user research practice. It's enabled our team to scale customer conversations without scaling a massive user research team, and it's really changed how we operate.”


Jon Dobrowolski


Product Leader, Core Experiences, Asana


### Brex


In one year, Brex scaled internal research participation from single-digit contributors to 100+ with Great Question. They democratized research by removing bottlenecks and empowering non-researchers to run studies through safe, repeatable processes.


> “Before we brought on Great Question, research at Brex was reserved for only the few people that knew how to use the tools, find participants and run studies. The number of people comfortable running research grew from single digits to over 100 people at Brex running research with Great Question.”


Nicolás Carey


VP, Product & Design, Brex


### Miro


Without strong research operations, even your biggest power users can be tough to recruit and manage as research participants. This was once the case for Miro, too many tools, not enough processes. So to consolidate their toolstack, simplify research operations, and save on costs, they switched to Great Question.


> “Great Question is built for the new generation of researchers. They're doing what other tools have traditionally tried, which is build an end-to-end workflow for UX research, but they're actually doing it in a way that's sensible to researchers. You can see by the amount of detailed features that, as a researcher, you have to smile because they really get it.”


Josh Morales


UX Research Manager, Miro


Read more


[Why Miro switched to Great Question](https://www.greatquestion.com/customers/miro) with Josh Morales


### ServiceNow


Great Question has helped A'verria and ServiceNow consolidate tools and accelerate research velocity, delivering research 6x faster and scaling to 300+ studies and 10,000 participants without sacrificing rigor.


> “We've been connected with Great Question for about four years, from the early conversations about the platform's vision and the future of research, to exploring how to make research more efficient, effective, and delightful. Seeing that vision come to life has built tremendous trust in the company, and that's why we became a customer.”


A'verria Martin


Senior Director, Product Research, Intelligence & Strategy, ServiceNow


### Simpson Strong-Tie


Recruiting B2B participants is tough. For Simpson Strong-Tie, the seasonal ebbs and flows of construction crank things up a notch. And their "Frankenstein of tools" wasn't helping. With Great Question, Kristine and her team have consolidated tools, simplified recruitment for hard-to-reach customers, and gotten more designers, PMs, and engineers involved in research.


> “Great Question is the do-it-all research tool that helps our software development team deliver findings and insights in half the time from recruitment, interviews, data analysis, video clips, and even incentives.”


Kristine Lemos


Senior UX Researcher, Simpson Strong-Tie


Read more


[Consolidating research tools & cutting time-to-insights in half](https://www.greatquestion.com/customers/simpson-strong-tie) with Kristine Lemos, Ian Wyosnick & Robert Frey


### Sinch


Tired of paying an arm and a leg for UserTesting and Dovetail, Nicki and the growing design team at Sinch switched to Great Question. So far, they've consolidated eight tools and saved 35% on costs while giving more cross-functional stakeholders the ability to access research insights and artifacts.


> “When we eliminated tools like UserTesting and Dovetail, we were able to do more with Great Question with the same amount of money. We could fund more incentives to customers, recruit more participants, and talk to more panels.”


Nicki Snyder


Head of Product Design, Sinch


Read more


[From "free-for-all" to all-in-one: How Sinch consolidated 8 research tools & saved 35%](https://www.greatquestion.com/customers/sinch) with Nicki Snyder & Stephanie Soo

Our[2025 State of Research Democratization Report](https://www.greatquestion.com/ux-research/democratization) shares what we learned: the good, the bad, and everything in between.
